method: scripts/ib-research/claim-check.js: the passage is copied verbatim from the live source text at the pinned revision; VERIFIED = every claim number in one sentence that shares >= 50% of the claim's content words

records.claim: The probes would be propelled by a square-kilometre array of 10 kW ground-based lasers with a combined output of up to 100 GW.
records.passage: They would be propelled by a square-kilometre array of 10 kW ground-based lasers with a combined output of up to 100 GW.

records.claim: To accelerate the 4 m sail at 10,000 Gs to 0.2 c requires combining optics which are approximately 3 kilometers in diameter.
records.passage: For example, to accelerate the previously mentioned 4 m sail at 10,000 Gs to 0.2 c requires combining optics which are approximately 3 kilometers in diameter to focus the laser light on the sail.

records.claim: The spacecraft will have to survive collisions with space dust; each square centimeter of frontal cross-section is expected to collide with about a thousand particles of size at least 0.1 μm.
records.passage: The spacecraft will have to survive collisions with space dust; Starshot expects each square centimeter of frontal cross-section to collide at high speed with about a thousand particles of size at least 0.1 μm.

records.claim: Milner placed the final mission cost at $5–10 billion.
records.passage: Milner placed the final mission cost at $5–10 billion, and estimated the first craft could launch by around 2036.

records.claim: In September 2025, Scientific American reported that the project was on hold indefinitely.
records.passage: In September 2025, Scientific American reported that the project was on hold indefinitely.

narration.text: Why a star probe needs 100 gigawatts of lasers.
Its sail must reach a fifth of light speed.
The probes would weigh grams, on ultra-thin sails.
Focusing that beam needs optics about 3 kilometres across.
Every square centimetre would hit about a thousand dust grains.
Estimates put the mission at $5 to 10 billion.
In 2025, the project was reported on hold indefinitely.
So reaching another star is possible on paper, and very hard in practice.
